items.headline: Campbell ordinance would require replacement housing when homes are demolished
items.summary: The October 27 agenda listed a Replacement Housing and Demolition Control Ordinance (PLN 202683) that sets replacement housing unit requirements tied to demolition. The item called for a recommendation of approval to the City Council, which could take it up in November. The same agenda listed a minor housing development permit and tentative subdivision map.

items.headline: Citywide residential parking rules rewrite: continuance to Nov. 9 requested
items.summary: The October 26 Planning Commission agenda listed a proposed ordinance to repeal and replace Sunnyvale's parking chapter (19.46) and amend the Downtown, Lawrence Station, El Camino Real and Dual Urban Opportunity Housing zoning chapters. The item carried a request for continuance to November 9, 2026, and the agenda does not confirm that the delay happened. The commission was to forward a recommendation to the City Council.

items.headline: Study session on replacing Hawthorn Avenue duplex with three townhomes
items.summary: The Planning Commission's October 26 special study session agenda listed a proposal to demolish a 1,360-square-foot duplex at 536 Hawthorn Avenue and build three townhome-style condominiums in one two-story building. The 0.29-acre R-3 lot would be subdivided into three parcels, and the city proposes treating the project as exempt from CEQA environmental review.

items.headline: Pruneyard asks to push back office tower deadlines to 2031
items.summary: The October 20 City Council agenda listed a public hearing on the Pruneyard Center Association's request to extend the phasing deadlines for Phases 3 and 4 to December 31, 2031. Those phases include a five-story office building, parking structure expansions and additional commercial buildings. The request also covers extending the tentative parcel map that would create a fourth parcel for the office building. The Planning Commission recommended that the council approve it.

items.headline: Palo Alto weighs up to $100M in electric bonds for grid upgrades
items.summary: The October 20 Finance Committee agenda listed a recommendation to the City Council on a resolution authorizing tax-exempt electric revenue bonds of up to $100 million to finance the Grid Modernization for Electrification project. The agenda also listed a review of proposed reserve categories and targets.

items.headline: Council agenda: child care partnership at Cubberley, Caltrain funding scenario
items.summary: The October 19 City Council agenda listed a Letter of Intent with Palo Alto Community Child Care for a long-term public-private partnership to expand child care at the Cubberley site. It also listed a Caltrain presentation on a framework for a "No External Funding Scenario" and a $15,000 Council Contingency allocation to the Know Your Neighbors Grant Program.
